subject: Post-demo: callable schema readiness & regression flags
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Kline <aisha.k@archimedes.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: callable schema readiness & regression flags

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the product demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

1) Model recommendations for initial benchmarks
   - Redwood-Res-7B (fp16 / q8) — baseline for throughput + structured output.
   - Redwood-OPT-30B-q8 — higher quality for slot-filling and few-shot JSON returns.

2) Focused evals we suggested
   - JSON schema compliance: 1k prompt set (see attached prompt_samples.csv) with fields: intent, slots, metadata.
   - Function-calling/retries: test 3 retry strategies (no-retry, idempotent-retry, backoff-with-de-dup) and measure duplicate side-effects.
   - Quality regression: run the new prompt set against your production sample (we asked for 500 anonymized records).

3) Action items (ownership + timing)
   - Aisha / Archimedes: share 500-sample anonymized payloads and a short list of non-idempotent endpoints by EOD Tue (14 Sep).
   - Camila (Solutions): provide the eval harness + schema_v1.json and a suggested runner for retries by Mon.
   - Sean (me): schedule a 30-min follow-up to finalize SLA/rollback triggers; draft included (SLA-draft-v1.pdf).

Attachments: prompt_samples.csv (prompt examples), SLA-draft-v1.pdf

Open questions we should confirm on the call:
- Do you expect any side-effects from retries (external webhook calls)?
- Are there internal rules for partial acceptances (e.g., allow missing optional slots)?

If that all looks right, Camila / Laura and I can run the Redwoods + OPT variants on a short benchmark and share a one-page results summary before the follow-up. Are you available Tue 14 Sep 10:00–11:00 PT?

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference


From: Aisha Kline <aisha.k@archimedes.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Pedro Gomes <pedro.g@archimedes.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:16:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: callable schema readiness & regression flags

Thanks Sean — great summary. Quick answers and a couple of clarifying asks: 

- We can deliver the 500 anonymized payloads by EOD Monday (we'll strip PII).
- We do have a handful of non-idempotent endpoints (billing webhook, provisioner). We will require an idempotency key for any retry path.

Two questions for the team: 
1) For the JSON schema compliance check, do you validate strictly (fail on extra fields) or do you allow permissive parsing with warnings? We need to know if Redwood's runner will reject responses or return them with a compliance score.
2) For function calling, how do you detect/handle duplicate side-effects if the model retries a call? In our stack we can accept retries only if an idempotency key is provided — is that something Redwood can surface from the outgoing function-call payloads?

Also, we have a tight timeline for Q4 pilot — an answer on the above two items would help our security and dev teams sign off. Tue 14 Sep 10:00 PT works for us. Please send an invite.

Best,
Aisha Kline
Head of Product
Archimedes AI

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: callable schema readiness & regression flags

Aisha — thanks for the quick turn. Short tech notes to answer the questions and set expectations before our Tue call: 

- Schema validation modes (what we'll run):
  * strict (fail on missing required fields OR type mismatch) — useful for gate checks.
  * tolerant (accept extra fields, score based on required-field presence) — useful for telemetry/gradual rollouts.
  We will produce a compliance report (pass/fail + per-field confidence). The harness will not auto-reject in tolerant mode; it will flag issues.

- Function-calling & duplicate side-effects:
  * Redwood's runtime includes an outbound call proxy that tags calls with an internal request_id and will surface the model-suggested idempotency_key when provided by the prompt/function payload.
  * For retries: our suggested default is backoff-with-de-dup (3 attempts) when idempotency_key exists. For non-idempotent endpoints we can run no-retry or require an explicit server-side confirm before re-attempt.

- Test harness & repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/archimedes-eval-harness (readme includes runner for strict/tolerant schema checks and retry simulators).

- Benchmarks we'll produce before the Tue call:
  1) Compliance pass-rate (strict) across Redwood-Res-7B and Redwood-OPT-30B-q8 on your anonymized 500 records.
  2) Mean latency and token cost per call.
  3) Retry-induced duplicate-call rate for the billing webhook simulation (we'll attach logs and de-dup markers).

Attachments included: schema_v1.json, eval-instructions.md

If that looks good I'll run the harness on a small internal sample tonight so we have a baseline report to share Monday morning.

Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
